title.narrative: Policy 1 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Jul 01, 2021 - Jan 31, 2026

description.narrative:
Action 1: Ministry of Finance approved and commenced implementation of the CRM Plan 2021-2026 to improve resiliency and efficiency of customs clearance procedures for cross-border trade by including reform measures to introduce e-payment, actions to proceed paperless customs, post-clearance audit, reduction of export documentation requirements, and introduction of valuation database. (Proof MOF letter certifying that the Finance Minister has approved the CRM Plan 2021-2026; certified copy of CRM Plan 2022; DOC letter certifying that DG, DOC accepted the implementation status report; certified copy of implementation status report) Target date: 2026-01-31
Action 2: DOC pilot-tested e-payment in at least one out of 10 major revenue-generating customs offices to reduce transaction time and costb (Proof: DOC letter confirming that DG, DOC ordered commencement of the pilot-test; and certified copy of the evaluation report including metadata and sample of e-payment transaction record) Target date: 2026-01-31
Action 3: DOC pilot-tested mandatory online submission of all documents for export in one out of the 10 major customs offices to promote paperless customs and facilitate export. (Proof: DOC letter confirming that DG, DOC ordered commencement of the pilot-test, and certified copy of the evaluation report including metadata) Target date: 2026-01-31
Action 4: DOC developed and operationalized an interface in ASYCUDA Worldc to receive from other government agencies licenses, permit, certificates, and other documents which are required for customs clearance through the Nepal National Single Window to promote paperless customs process within the government. (Proof: DOC letter confirming that the DG, DOC ordered development of ASYCUDA World interface; and certified operationalization status report with metadata demonstrating submissions to ASYCUDA World) Target date: 2026-01-31
Action 5: Cabinet approved the amendment to the Customs Regulation 2007 on the reduction of export documentation requirement of packing list to ease the customs clearance process.f (Proof: DOC letter confirming that the Cabinet approved the amendment and Gazette Notification of the Amended Customs Regulation Act 2007) Target date: 2026-01-31
Action 1: DOC will establish and commence operation of an e-payment facility in at least the 10 major customs offices. (Proof: DOC letter confirming that DG, DOC ordered to establish and commence operation of e-payment facility in the customs offices; copy of public notification of commencement of policy action; and a certified copy of evaluation report including metadata and sample of e-payment transaction record) Target date: 2025-07-31

Action 1: Cabinet approved the TLP which became effective in 2022 to enhance trade competitiveness through reduced cost of trade logistics, improved trade facilitation, improved domestic supply chain management, and quality employment generation. The objective will be achieved by TLP including reform measures to introduce (i) logistics infrastructure master plan, (ii) PPP guidelines, (iii) technical standards of logistics infrastructure and equipment, (iv) grading system, (v) logistics information portal, and (vi) guidelines on government support to small and medium-sized logistics enterprises. (Proof: MOICS letter confirming that the Cabinet approved the TLP; and certified copy of TLP) Target date: 2023-01-31

title.narrative: Policy 2 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Jul 01, 2021 - Jan 31, 2023

description.narrative:
Policy 2: Logistics sector developed and strengthened NA
Action 2: MOICS established an institutional arrangement, which began functioning to enhance inter-Ministerial coordination on policy reforms in logistics sectorl and began functioning with the first Implementation Committee Meeting completed. The institutional arrangements include (i) the Board of Trade chaired by the Minister of MOICS to provide strategic and policy guidance; (ii) the Coordination Committee chaired by the Chief Secretary to facilitate inter-ministry coordination and ensure alignment of TLDP with other government plans, policies and strategies; and (iii) the Implementation Committee chaired by the Secretary MOICS.n (Proof: MOICS letter confirming the establishment of institutional arrangements; and certified minutes of the first Implementation Committee Meeting) Target date: 2023-01-31
Action 3: MOICS approved a sequenced, time-bound Work Plan for TLP. The Work Plan included preparation and implementation of infrastructure master plan, PPP guidelines, technical standards, grading system, logistics information portal, capacity development plan for small and medium-sized logistics enterprisesp, as well as GESI Needs Assessment for logistics infrastructure and GESI Responsive Guidelines for the logistics sector. (Proof: MOICS letter certifying that the Minister approved the Work Plan; and a certified copy of the Work Plan) Target date: 2023-01-31
Action 1: MOICS will approve and commence implementation of climate and disaster-resilient responsive logistics infrastructure master plan for 2025-2029 for a systematic and coordinated development of logistics infrastructure across different transport modes, effective last-mile connectivity, and promotion of private sector investment.i (Proof: MOICS letter confirming that Commerce Minister has approved and commenced implementation; certified copy of the logistics infrastructure master plan; and FY2025 budget indicating public sector logistics projects) Target date: 2025-07-31
